output.executive_summary:
The Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM), a Syrian-led nonprofit registered in Türkiye with legal personality, is submitting a concept note as lead applicant for Lot 3 of EuropeAid/185831/DD/ACT/SY — Promotion of and support to media freedom and pluralism in Syria. CSIM's core mandate is a direct match for the lot's three priorities: strengthening independent Syrian media, protecting journalists and media workers, and building public awareness of media freedom. With operational nodes in Istanbul, Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli, a vetted network of Syrian journalists and fact-checkers, and multi-platform Arabic and Kurdish content production, CSIM brings field-tested infrastructure that few applicants can replicate for this specific context.

CSIM's track record demonstrates consistent delivery against EU and US donor frameworks. Four sub-million-EUR grants have been completed on time with no audit qualifications, including a lead-applicant role on a small EU project in 2023 and a co-applicant role on a USAID award in 2022. Donors have included SIDA (two grants, 2021–2024), Free Press Unlimited, and Internews. A clean KPMG Türkiye audit for 2024 is available, and audited financial statements can be provided on request. CSIM's registration in Türkiye qualifies it for the 100% EU co-financing rate under the corrigendum, eliminating the need to source external co-financing beyond its own reserves, which materially strengthens the budget case.

The key win-themes for this bid are: (1) Syrian-led identity and deep field presence across conflict-affected governorates, giving CSIM unmatched contextual legitimacy; (2) proven information-integrity and anti-disinformation programming that directly addresses the EU's digital-freedoms priority under the Human Rights and Democracy Thematic Programme 2025–2027; (3) multilingual capacity in Arabic, Kurdish, English, and Turkish enabling inclusive outreach to minority communities; and (4) a lean, cost-effective organisational model that maximises programme spend within the fixed EUR 675,000 grant envelope. Two administrative risks — PADOR registration not yet complete and the absence of a signed co-applicant commitment letter — are actively being resolved and must be closed before the 18 May 2026 deadline.
technical_approach: Context analysis and needs assessment. CSIM will open the action with a structured rapid media-ecosystem assessment covering all governorates where it maintains field nodes — Qamishli (northeast), Gaziantep (northwest corridor), and Erbil (diaspora hub) — supplemented by remote key-informant interviews with Syrian journalists currently operating inside Syria. The assessment will map: (a) the number and type of active independent media outlets by geography; (b) documented threats to journalists including detention, harassment, and digital surveillance since December 2024; (c) gaps in editorial capacity, safety protocols, and digital-security literacy; and (d) audience access to independent information, disaggregated by gender, age, and ethnicity. Findings will be validated through a participatory workshop with CSIM's existing network of approximately 40 vetted contributors and will feed directly into the action's intervention logic, ensuring the design is evidence-based and responsive to the post-Assad transitional context.

Component 1 — Strengthening independent media and journalists. CSIM will deliver a structured capacity-development programme targeting Syrian newsrooms operating inside Syria and in the diaspora. This will include: (a) a modular editorial-coaching curriculum covering investigative reporting, source verification, fact-checking methodology, and editorial independence standards, delivered in Arabic and Kurdish through a blended in-person and online format; (b) small equipment and connectivity grants to up to eight priority newsrooms identified through the needs assessment, enabling reliable publication and broadcast; and (c) a peer-learning exchange programme connecting Syrian journalists with regional and international counterparts. CSIM's existing editorial-coaching infrastructure, developed under SIDA and Free Press Unlimited funding, will be adapted and scaled rather than built from scratch, reducing mobilisation time and cost. All training materials will be made openly available in Arabic and Kurdish to maximise reach beyond direct participants.

Component 2 — Protection of journalists, bloggers, and media workers. CSIM will establish a structured journalist-protection support mechanism comprising three elements. First, a digital-security training programme — delivered in partnership with a specialist EU-eligible INGO to be confirmed as co-applicant — covering encrypted communications, operational security, and online harassment response, targeting at least 60 journalists and media workers across the action period. Second, a rapid-response small-grants facility providing emergency support to journalists facing acute threats, with a streamlined assessment and disbursement process drawing on CSIM's existing financial-management systems. Third, a documentation and monitoring function tracking threats to media workers in Syria, producing quarterly public reports that feed into international advocacy. CSIM acknowledges that physical-protection programming requires specialist partner capacity; the co-applicant INGO will hold lead responsibility for this sub-component, and the partnership scope will be formalised in the commitment letter currently under negotiation.

Component 3 — Public awareness and inclusive debate on media freedom. CSIM will design and implement a multi-platform public-awareness campaign on the centrality of media freedom in Syria's transitional period. Campaign content will be produced in Arabic and Kurdish across social media, radio, and community platforms, drawing on CSIM's established multi-platform content-production capability. The campaign will include: (a) a series of short documentary features profiling Syrian journalists and their role in accountability; (b) community listening sessions in at least four governorates, facilitated by CSIM's field nodes, to generate two-way dialogue rather than one-way broadcasting; and (c) a media-literacy module integrated into the Component 1 training curriculum, equipping journalists themselves to advocate for press freedom with their audiences. Gender balance in featured voices and Kurdish-language content will be explicit production requirements, directly addressing cross-cutting obligations.

Cross-cutting issues integration. Gender equality will be mainstreamed throughout all components: training cohorts will target a minimum 40% female participation; the needs assessment will include a gender-disaggregated analysis of threats faced by women journalists; and campaign content will actively feature women media workers. Disability inclusion will be addressed through accessible formats for all training materials and captioned video content. Minority rights and youth engagement are structurally embedded through Kurdish-language programming and a deliberate focus on recruiting young journalists (under 30) into the capacity-development programme. Environmental considerations will be addressed through a preference for digital-first delivery modalities, minimising travel-related emissions, and a light-footprint field-operations approach consistent with CSIM's existing operational model.

Risk management and assumptions. The principal risks identified for this action are: (a) deteriorating security conditions in Syria limiting field access — mitigated by CSIM's established remote-delivery protocols and field-node network; (b) digital-surveillance threats to programme participants — mitigated by integrating operational-security protocols into all field activities from day one; (c) delay in formalising the co-applicant partnership — mitigated by the current active negotiation and the fallback option of engaging the INGO as a subcontractor if a commitment letter cannot be secured before submission; (d) PADOR registration not completed before the deadline — mitigated by the registration having been initiated on 21 April 2026 with active follow-up (see next steps); and (e) currency and banking risk given Akbank TRY and EUR accounts — mitigated by maintaining EUR-denominated project accounts and applying EU standard exchange-rate rules. Key assumptions include: continued access to northeast Syria through the Qamishli node; stability of the transitional Syrian government's policy environment toward independent media; and availability of CSIM's core staff throughout the action period.

Work plan and deliverables. The action is planned over 24 months. Months 1–3 will cover mobilisation, needs assessment, and co-applicant onboarding. Months 4–12 will deliver the first cycle of editorial coaching, digital-security training, and campaign production. Months 13–20 will deliver the second training cycle, the rapid-response facility, and mid-term documentation reports. Months 21–24 will cover final campaign outputs, evaluation, and knowledge-product dissemination. Key deliverables include: one media-ecosystem assessment report; training of a minimum 80 journalists and media workers across both components; support to a minimum eight newsrooms; four quarterly threat-monitoring reports; one multi-platform public-awareness campaign with documented reach metrics; and a final evaluation report with lessons-learned documentation for public dissemination.

Quality assurance and monitoring. CSIM will apply a results-based monitoring framework aligned with the EU's standard logical-framework approach, with indicators defined at output, outcome, and impact levels. A dedicated monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) focal point within CSIM's Istanbul office will maintain a live indicator-tracking dashboard updated monthly. Quarterly internal review meetings will assess progress against the work plan and trigger adaptive management decisions where needed. An independent mid-term review will be commissioned at month 12, and a final external evaluation at month 22, both with terms of reference approved by the EU Delegation. CSIM's KPMG-audited financial-management systems will be applied throughout, with expenditure reporting against EU standard cost categories and a zero-tolerance policy on ineligible costs. All financial records will be maintained in EUR and made available for EU audit or verification on request.

18 May 2026

To the Evaluation Committee,
European Union Delegation to Syria
Call for Proposals EuropeAid/185831/DD/ACT/SY
Lot 3 — Promotion of and support to media freedom and pluralism in Syria

Dear Members of the Evaluation Committee,

The Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM) is pleased to submit this concept note in response to the European Commission's Call for Proposals EuropeAid/185831/DD/ACT/SY, Lot 3: Promotion of and support to media freedom and pluralism in Syria. CSIM is a Syrian-led nonprofit organisation registered in Türkiye with full legal personality, operating since 2018 with a mandate that is directly and exclusively aligned with the three priorities of Lot 3. Our field nodes in Istanbul, Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli give us active operational reach across the Syrian media landscape at precisely the moment when the post-Assad transitional period demands credible, independent, and locally rooted support to freedom of expression. We believe this combination of Syrian-led identity, field infrastructure, and proven donor-compliance capacity makes CSIM a strong and appropriate lead applicant for this grant.

CSIM has delivered four international grants on time and without audit qualification, including grants from SIDA (two awards, 2021–2024), Free Press Unlimited (2022), and Internews (subaward, 2023), as well as serving as lead applicant on a small EU-funded project in 2023 and co-applicant on a USAID award in 2022. Our 2024 financial statements have been audited by KPMG Türkiye with a clean opinion, and our financial-management systems are fully aligned with EU standard cost-eligibility rules. As an organisation registered in Türkiye, CSIM qualifies for the 100% EU co-financing rate under the corrigendum to these guidelines, enabling the full EUR 675,000 grant to be directed to programme activities. Our proposed action under Lot 3 will strengthen independent Syrian newsrooms through structured editorial coaching and equipment support, protect journalists and media workers through digital-security training and a rapid-response support mechanism delivered in partnership with a specialist EU-eligible organisation, and build public awareness of media freedom through a multi-platform Arabic and Kurdish campaign reaching audiences across Syria's diverse communities. All activities are grounded in a rapid media-ecosystem assessment that CSIM will conduct at the outset of the action, ensuring the intervention logic is evidence-based and responsive to the evolving transitional context.

We respectfully request that the Evaluation Committee consider this concept note for pre-selection to the full-application stage. CSIM is committed to full transparency throughout the evaluation process and stands ready to provide any additional documentation, clarification, or supporting evidence that the Contracting Authority may require. We are grateful for the European Commission's continued commitment to Syrian civil society and to the protection of media freedom as a cornerstone of Syria's democratic transition, and we look forward to the opportunity to contribute to these objectives as a trusted implementing partner.

Yours sincerely,

[Name of Executive Director / Authorised Representative]
Executive Director
Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM)
Istanbul, Türkiye
